rows.en: Slowly becoming a puddle in the corner.
rows.reason: Plain, natural melting-in-the-heat image; 'ichibi' (pool) is a fair hyperbolic stand-in for puddle and 'ekhoneni' keeps the corner.

rows.en: The sky picked a vibe and the vibe is shrug.
rows.draft: Isibhakabhaka sikhethe i-vibe futhi i-vibe iwukunyusa amahlombe.
rows.reason: Code-switched 'i-vibe' matches the confirmed 'I-vibe yi-beige'; 'iwukunyusa amahlombe' (is the raising of shoulders) is understandable and the deadpan carries.

rows.en: Hair plans: cancelled.
rows.reason: 'zikhanselelwe' is the applied-passive (cancelled for/at someone); the plain passive 'zikhanselwe' is what a speaker says. Rest is fine.
rows.rewrite: Izinhlelo zezinwele: zikhanselwe.

rows.en: The duvet understood the assignment.
rows.reason: 'Understood the assignment' is an idiom for nailing it; 'iyiqondile into edingekayo' (understood the needed thing) is a stiff literal rendering and the joke goes flat.
rows.rewrite: I-duvet yenze kahle kakhulu umsebenzi wayo.

rows.en: The garden is somewhere out there. We trust the process.
rows.reason: 'Ikhona ngaphandle' drops 'somewhere', which is the whole point (nobody can see the garden); 'Sithemba inqubo' is a stiff calque of 'trust the process'.
rows.rewrite: Ingadi isendaweni ethile ngaphandle. Sithembela enqubweni.

rows.en: Perfect excuse to cancel plans.
rows.reason: Natural and clear; 'khansela izinhlelo' matches the app's usage. 'Esihle' is a touch softer than 'perfect' but the warm remark works.

rows.en: This is why we live in South Africa.
rows.reason: Same 'Yingakho...' construction as the confirmed Noah line; simple, warm, a speaker could have written it.

rows.en: It is what it is.
rows.reason: 'Kuyilokho okuyikho' is a word-for-word calque of 'it is what it is'; a speaker would say 'Kunjalo nje'.
rows.rewrite: Kunjalo nje.

rows.en: Sky's looking moody. Could escalate.
rows.reason: Reads naturally; 'sithukuthele' (angry) is a slightly stronger sky mood than 'moody' but fits, and 'kungakhula' (it could grow) carries 'could escalate'.

rows.en: Hold onto your hat! And your kids.
rows.reason: Natural imperative with a good tag; 'Nabantwana bakho' (and your children) lands the joke.

rows.en: Not a hairstyle in sight. Just survivors.
rows.draft: Akukho sitayela sezinwele esibonwayo. Abasindile kuphela.
rows.reason: 'Akukho sitayela sezinwele esibonwayo' mirrors the confirmed 'Akukho lifu elibonwayo'; 'Abasindile kuphela' gives the dry turn.

rows.en: Clear-ish night. Don't hold us to the stars.
rows.reason: 'Obuhle-ish' sticks an English suffix on a Zulu word and 'buhle' means nice, not clear (the app uses 'obucacile/obucwebile'); 'Ungasibambi ezinkanyezini' is a calque of 'hold us to' that does not mean that.
rows.rewrite: Ubusuku obucacile, cishe. Ungazithembi kakhulu izinkanyezi.

rows.en: A proper good one. Don't waste it.
rows.reason: 'Olungcono' (the better one) has no noun to hang on, and 'ngcono' means better, not good; a speaker would name the day.
rows.rewrite: Usuku oluhle ngempela. Ungalumoshi.

rows.en: Unplug the things. The sky has plans.
rows.draft: Susa izinto eziphakwe ku-elektriki. Isibhakabhaka sinezinhlelo.
rows.reason: 'Eziphakwe ku-elektriki' means things served on electricity ('phakwa' is to be dished up); unplug needs 'susa/khipha' and electricity is 'ugesi'. The second sentence is fine.
rows.rewrite: Susa izinto zikagesi kugesi. Isibhakabhaka sinezinhlelo.

rows.en: The street signs gave up.
rows.reason: Short, natural, 'ziyekile' (have stopped/given up) personifies the signs the way the native lines do.

rows.en: This is not what the tourism brochure promised.
rows.reason: Natural complaint structure ('akukhona okwethenjiswa...'); 'incwadi yokuvakasha' is a little loose for a brochure but understood.

rows.en: The shower was the highlight. It is downhill from here.
rows.draft: Ishawa kwakuyinto enhle. Konke kuya phansi manje.
rows.reason: 'Ishawa kwakuyinto enhle' has an agreement slip (ishawa takes 'yayi-') and 'a nice thing' loses 'highlight', which the 'downhill' turn depends on.
rows.rewrite: Ishawa yayiyinto engcono kunazo zonke. Konke kuya phansi manje.

rows.en: Tile floors are tonight's villain. Wear something on your feet.
rows.draft: Ama-tile floors yi-villain yanamuhla kusihlwa. Gqoka okuthile ezinyaweni.
rows.reason: Raw English chunks 'tile floors' (doubly plural) and 'yi-villain' where isiZulu has plain words; the natives fixed the same kind of line by replacing the English phrase.
rows.rewrite: Phansi kwama-tile kuyisitha sanamuhla kusihlwa. Gqoka okuthile ezinyaweni.

rows.en: Shorts weather? This is underwear weather.
rows.draft: Isimo sezulu samabhulukwe amafushane? Lesi isimo sezulu samangisi.
rows.reason: 'Amangisi' is not an underwear word I can attest, so the punchline breaks; the set-up (amabhulukwe amafushane) is fine and 'Lesi isimo' also needs 'yisimo'.
rows.rewrite: Isimo sezulu samabhulukwe amafushane? Lesi yisimo sezulu sezingubo zangaphakathi.

rows.en: Boerie roll for breakfast? On a weekend? Acceptable.
rows.reason: Natural code-switching (iboerie roll, ibhulakufesi), 'ngempelasonto' is the right weekend word, 'iyamukeleka' gives the dry verdict.

rows.en: Beach or braai? Yes.
rows.reason: Short and exact: 'ibhishi', 'ukosa' as the app uses it, and the 'Yebo' answer to an either/or lands as in English.

rows.en: Beautiful and terrifying in equal measure.
rows.reason: 'Kuhle futhi kwesabisa ngokulinganayo' is clean and natural; 'esabisa' is already used in the confirmed lines and the warm awe comes through.

rows.en: Even the shade is sweating.
rows.reason: Natural: ukujuluka is the everyday word for sweating (the confirmed lines use 'Awujuluki'), and 'ngisho nomthunzi' keeps the personification.

rows.en: Looks cold-ish. The thermometer's keeping us guessing.
rows.reason: Reads naturally and 'isenza siqagele' carries 'keeping us guessing'; the '-ish' hedge is lost but the second sentence supplies the doubt, like the kept 'Kubukeka kunamafu. Imithombo ayivumelani.'

rows.en: The N1 is now a waterpark.
rows.reason: Plain copula with a code-switched loan ('yi-waterpark'), the same pattern natives kept in 'isiyi-cooler box'; the joke carries.

rows.en: Clouds looking proper suspicious.
rows.reason: 'Abukeka esolisa ngempela' is correct (participial after bukeka) and 'esolisa' matches the confirmed 'okusolisayo'; ngempela handles 'proper'.

rows.en: The fog doesn't care about your schedule.
rows.reason: 'Ayikhathaleli' is the right negative of khathalela and the fog-as-character joke lands; 'isheduli' is a normal everyday loan.

rows.en: The puddle was deeper than it looked. It's always deeper.
rows.draft: Isiziba sasijule kunalokho ebesibukeka ngakho. Sihlala sijule.
rows.reason: 'Isiziba' is a deep pool or pond, not a street puddle, so 'deeper than it looked' goes flat; the comparative 'kunalokho ebesibukeka ngakho' also sounds translated. Use plain 'amanzi'.
rows.rewrite: Amanzi ayejule kunalokho abukeka ngakho. Njalo ajule kakhulu.

rows.en: The sky's undecided. So are we.
rows.reason: 'Asinqumanga' matches the confirmed 'asikwazi ukunquma' and 'Nathi futhi' is a natural dry second beat.

rows.en: 50/50 on the rain. Bring a jacket, just in case.
rows.draft: I-50/50 emvuleni. Thatha ibhantshi, uma kwenzeka.
rows.reason: 'I-50/50 emvuleni' reads 'in the rain', not 'on the rain'; and 'uma kwenzeka' is 'if it happens' where the confirmed 'just in case' phrase is 'uma kungenzeka'.
rows.rewrite: Imvula iyi-50/50. Thatha ibhantshi, uma kungenzeka.

rows.en: Good soup weather, not gonna lie.
rows.reason: 'Isimo sezulu esihle sesobho' mirrors the confirmed 'Isimo sezulu esihle sefilimu yesabisayo'; 'not gonna lie' is dropped, as natives allowed in other kept lines, so it reads a little plain.

rows.en: Don't trust those clouds. They're plotting.
rows.reason: 'Ungawathembi lawo mafu' is correct and natural; 'ayaceba' (they scheme) keeps the clouds-as-characters joke, though 'aceba okuthile' would be fuller.

rows.en: Even the shade is warm. Good luck out there.
rows.reason: Clean and natural; 'Inhlanhla enhle' is the confirmed good-luck phrase and 'ufudumele' fits 'warm'.

rows.en: Wait it out indoors. The mountains aren't going anywhere.
rows.reason: 'Lindela' means to expect or wait for something, and 'wait it out' needs 'linda ... kuze kudlule'; 'phakathi' alone is 'in the middle', and the app's confirmed form is 'ngaphakathi'. The mountain beat is fine.
rows.rewrite: Linda ngaphakathi kuze kudlule. Izintaba aziyi ndawo.

rows.en: Postcard weather. You're welcome.
rows.reason: Short and natural; 'se-postcard' is the same code-switched loan style natives kept elsewhere, and 'Wamukelekile' is the confirmed 'you're welcome'.

rows.en: Your jacket has a jacket. It's that kind of day.
rows.reason: Grammatical and natural ('linebhantshi', 'usuku olunjalo'); ijazi/ibhantshi are two different words, so the English repetition gag is a little softer but the layering still reads.

rows.en: Cloudy-ish. Don't bet the braai on it.
rows.reason: 'Ungabhejeli ukosa kukho' is garbled: 'kukho' has no referent, so 'bet the braai on it' does not come through. Use 'ungabheji ukosa kulokhu'.
rows.rewrite: Kunamafu, cishe. Ungabheji ukosa kulokhu.

rows.en: Everyone's suddenly your friend when you have a pool.
rows.reason: Natural and correct ('bangabangane', 'unepuli'); the word for 'suddenly' is missing so the turn is softer, but the meaning and tone come through.

rows.en: Today's forecast: medium rare.
rows.reason: 'Isibikezelo sanamuhla' is correct and 'medium rare' is the loan people actually say for steak, so the heat joke lands.

rows.en: Even the weather apps are arguing about this one.
rows.reason: Natural code-switch ('ama-app ezulu') with the right concord, and 'ayaphikisana ngalokhu' is plain and idiomatic.

rows.en: Might spit a bit. Might not bother.
rows.reason: 'Kungakhihliza' for rain 'spitting' is not a word I can confirm as light rain and risks a near-miss; the app's attested form is 'kungase line'. 'Kungase kungahluphi' is also a stiff double potential.
rows.rewrite: Kungase line kancane. Kungase kungazihluphi.

rows.en: Not the time for hero moves, hey.
rows.reason: 'Sokuqhawe' is not a form: iqhawe is 'hero' and the abstract is 'ubuqhawe', so 'isikhathi sokuqhawe' is malformed. The natural idiom is 'ukuzenza iqhawe'.
rows.rewrite: Akusona isikhathi sokuzenza iqhawe, hey.

rows.en: Joburg drivers are panicking already.
rows.reason: 'Sebeyesaba' is a garbled mix of tense markers, and it says 'afraid', not 'panicking'. Plain 'sebesaba kakade' says they are already scared.
rows.rewrite: Abashayeli baseJoburg sebesaba kakade.

rows.en: Bloemfontein at 6am: jersey, gown, scarf, takkies, and a brave face.
rows.draft: EBloemfontein ngo-6 ekuseni: i-jersey, i-gown, i-scarf, ama-takkies, nobuso obunesibindi.
rows.reason: A list of everyday loans in the same style as the kept 'I-weather yokubilisa i-kettle kabili'; 'ngo-6 ekuseni' and 'nobuso obunesibindi' are natural and the list-then-brave-face turn survives.

rows.en: Your excuse to stay inside just expired.
rows.draft: Isizathu sakho sokuhlala ngaphakathi sisanda kuphelelwa.
rows.reason: 'Sisanda kuphelelwa' means 'has just run out of (something)'; it needs an object ('yisikhathi') to mean expired. Use 'sisanda kuphela' for 'has just ended'.
rows.rewrite: Isizathu sakho sokuhlala ngaphakathi sisanda kuphela.

rows.en: Not a cloud. Just you and the Southern Cross.
rows.draft: Akukho lifu. Nguwe neSiphambano saseNingizimu kuphela.
rows.reason: Plain, clean and dry: 'Akukho lifu' echoes the confirmed 'Akukho lifu elibonwayo', and the 'you and the Southern Cross' turn carries over.

rows.en: The trees are doing involuntary yoga.
rows.reason: 'engafuneki' means unwanted/not needed, not involuntary; the joke is the trees being forced into poses, which a speaker would say with 'ngenkani'.
rows.rewrite: Izihlahla zenza i-yoga ngenkani.

rows.en: Perfect weather for existing without enthusiasm.
rows.draft: Isimo sezulu esihle sokuphila ngaphandle kwentshisekelo.
rows.reason: Understood, but 'ngaphandle kwentshisekelo' (without zeal) is heavy and stiff for a lazy-day quip; a speaker would use the everyday 'umdlandla'.
rows.rewrite: Isimo sezulu esihle sokuphila nje ungenamdlandla.

rows.en: SPF 50 or regret it by tonight.
rows.reason: 'uzozisola' is the right word for regret and the noma-warning matches the confirmed sunscreen lines; short and natural.

rows.en: Perfect weather for a Woolies run and Netflix.
rows.reason: Same frame as the confirmed 'Isimo sezulu esihle sefilimu yesabisayo'; Woolies and Netflix stay as natural code-switches, 'run' is dropped but the cosy errand-plus-couch picture comes through.

rows.en: Even the cattle on the N1 are huddled like they paid for it.
rows.draft: Ngisho nezinkomo eziku-N1 zibuthene sengathi zikhokhele indawo.
rows.reason: 'ku-N1' follows the confirmed 'ku-N2' pattern and 'zikhokhele indawo' (as if they paid for a spot) carries the huddle joke naturally.

rows.en: Stay hydrated or become a biltong.
rows.reason: 'noma ube yi-biltong' is correct and funny as is; 'Hlala unamanzi' (keep water with you) reads naturally for stay hydrated.

rows.en: Water consumption: yes. All of it.
rows.reason: Deadpan yebo/konke list-answer works the same way as the English; plain 'Ukuphuza amanzi' is less officious than 'consumption' but still dry ('wonke' would agree with amanzi, 'konke' is acceptable as all of it).

rows.en: Somewhere a weather reporter is living their best life.
rows.draft: Endaweni ethile umethuli wezindaba zesimo sezulu uphila kahle.
rows.reason: 'uphila kahle' only means is doing well/healthy, so the 'living their best life' idiom is gone; 'umethuli wezindaba zesimo sezulu' is also a long, stiff title.
rows.rewrite: Endaweni ethile umuntu obika isimo sezulu uphila impilo emnandi.

rows.en: Kite surfers are having the time of their lives.
rows.reason: Natural and warm with 'i-kite' as a loan; 'bajabulile kakhulu' flattens 'time of their lives' to very happy, but it still reads joyful.

rows.en: Sunscreen budget: higher than your data bill.
rows.draft: Isabiwezimali sesivikelo selanga: siphezulu kunebhili yakho yedatha.
rows.reason: 'isabiwezimali' is not the usual word for budget (that is 'isabelomali') and is stiff here; in everyday speech people just say 'i-budget'. The rest of the comparison is fine.
rows.rewrite: I-budget yesivikelo selanga: iphezulu kunebhili yakho yedatha.

rows.en: The UV index is higher than your expectations.
rows.reason: 'iphezulu kunalokho okulindele' is grammatical and keeps the high-versus-expectations play; 'I-UV index' is a natural code-switch.

rows.en: The Helderberg is showing off today.
rows.reason: Place name stays, 'iziqhayisa' echoes the confirmed show-off lines; 'iyaziqhayisa' is the more usual present but this stands.

rows.en: The sky's on mute. Nobody's complaining.
rows.reason: 'sithulile' plus 'Akekho okhonondayo' is natural and dry; the tech image of mute is lost, but the quiet-sky humour still lands.

rows.en: The sun doesn't care about your plans.
rows.reason: 'alikhathali' reads as 'is not tired' (ukukhathala); caring about something is 'ukukhathalela', and 'anginandaba' is the everyday way to say I don't care.
rows.rewrite: Ilanga alinandaba nezinhlelo zakho.

rows.en: Kuier weather. Get the people together.
rows.reason: Natural; the natives themselves swap Afrikaans 'lekker' for Zulu, so dropping 'kuier' for 'sokuhlangana' fits, though the kuier flavour thins.

rows.en: The bins are on an adventure again.
rows.reason: 'asohambweni futhi' (on a trip again) is idiomatic and the bins-as-travellers joke comes through; 'amabhini' is the plain loan.

rows.en: Trust issues with the sky today.
rows.reason: Understandable and dry as a fragment; 'Inkinga yokuthemba' is a slightly literal rendering of trust issues, but nothing is wrong.

rows.en: Probably a scorcher. A hat's not a bad idea.
rows.draft: Cishe usuku olushisayo. Isigqoko asilona icebo elibi.
rows.reason: Follows the confirmed 'Cishe usuku olumanzi' pattern; 'asilona icebo elibi' keeps the understatement of 'not a bad idea'.

rows.en: Cloud's the call. With an asterisk.
rows.reason: 'nophawu' is just a mark/sign, so the asterisk (the small-print caveat) is lost, and 'yiwo umbono' (is the opinion) is a vague stand-in for 'the call'.
rows.rewrite: Isibikezelo: amafu. Nge-asterisk.

rows.en: The fridge is the coolest room in the house.
rows.draft: Ifriji iyindawo epholile kunayo yonke endlini.
rows.reason: Clean comparative, 'iyindawo epholile kunayo yonke' agrees properly and 'indawo' for room is fine; reads as something a person would say.

rows.en: Even the weather can't be bothered today.
rows.draft: Ngisho nesimo sezulu asikwazi ukuziphatha namuhla.
rows.reason: 'asikwazi ukuziphatha' means can't behave itself, a different joke from can't be bothered.
rows.rewrite: Ngisho nesimo sezulu asifuni ukuzikhathaza namuhla.

rows.en: Whoever has a pool today is your new best friend.
rows.draft: Noma ngubani onepuli namuhla ngumngane wakho omusha omkhulu.
rows.reason: 'Noma ngubani onepuli' and 'umngane omkhulu' (best friend, as in the confirmed heater line) are exactly how people speak; warm and natural.

rows.en: The chops are calling. So is the chair.
rows.reason: Concord slip: 'nawo' agrees with ama-chop, but isihlalo (chair) takes 'naso'; as written the chair half of the joke is ungrammatical.
rows.rewrite: Ama-chop ayabiza. Nesihlalo naso siyabiza.

rows.en: The ozone layer called. It's on leave.
rows.reason: 'Ishayile' means 'has hit/struck', not 'has phoned'; a speaker says 'ishayele (ucingo)' for a call. 'Iku-leave' is fine as a code-switch.
rows.rewrite: I-ozone layer ishayele ucingo. Iku-leave.

rows.en: The weather gods are showing off.
rows.reason: Grammatical and warm; 'iyaziqhayisa' matches the confirmed 'imvelo iyaziqhayisa', and the gods-of-weather personification carries over.

rows.en: The wipers are on max and it's still not enough.
rows.reason: Plain, natural; 'aku-max' mirrors the confirmed 'liku-airplane mode' and 'akwanele' is how a speaker would say 'not enough'.

rows.en: The dog is staring at the rain like it's a personal insult.
rows.draft: Inja ibheka imvula sengathi inhlamba yomuntu siqu.
rows.reason: 'Sengathi' + noun needs the copula ('sengathi iyinhlamba'); without it the clause is incomplete. The image of the dog and the personal insult is good.
rows.rewrite: Inja ibheka imvula sengathi iyinhlamba yomuntu siqu.

rows.en: Don't even think about driving somewhere.
rows.reason: 'Ngisho' is followed by the na- form ('ngisho nokushayela', as in the confirmed 'ngisho nezaba zakho'), not 'ngisho ngokushayela'; the word order is translated-sounding.
rows.rewrite: Ungacabangi nokushayela ndawo.

rows.en: Grey vibes. The sky matched my Monday.
rows.draft: I-grey vibes. Isibhakabhaka sifana noMsombuluko wami.
rows.reason: Natural two-beat remark; 'sifana noMsombuluko wami' is correct and the Monday-grey mood comes through; 'i-vibes' is attested in the confirmed lines.

rows.en: Weather's being more indecisive than you at Spur.
rows.draft: Isimo sezulu asikwazi ukuzinquma njengawe eSpur.
rows.reason: The comparative is lost: 'njengawe' means 'like you', not 'more indecisive than you'. 'Ukuzinquma' is also stiffer than the confirmed 'ukunquma'.
rows.rewrite: Isimo sezulu asikwazi ukunquma kudlula wena eSpur.

rows.en: Good day for a walk, bad day for a tan.
rows.reason: 'Lokushisa' means 'for being hot/heating', not 'for a tan'; the meaning has drifted. A tan/sunburn from the sun is 'ukushiswa yilanga'.
rows.rewrite: Usuku oluhle lokuhamba, olubi lokushiswa yilanga.

rows.en: Not Instagram weather. Not the end of the world.
rows.draft: Akusona isimo sezulu se-Instagram. Akusikho ukuphela komhlaba.
rows.reason: Dry understatement kept intact; 'akusona ... akusikho' is the same negative copula pattern as the confirmed 'akusikho isifiso'.

rows.en: The clouds are here but they're not doing anything.
rows.reason: Short, idiomatic, 'awenzi lutho' is exactly how a speaker says it; the dry deadpan survives.

rows.en: Probably quiet skies. We're fairly sure.
rows.reason: Natural hedge; 'cishe' and 'siqinisekile cishe' echo the confirmed lines and 'izulu elithulile' agrees correctly.

rows.en: Don't touch the seatbelt buckle. Trust us.
rows.reason: 'Ibhande lokuvikela' is a stiff made-up descriptive term for a seatbelt; speakers just say 'i-seatbelt', as natives kept loans like i-geyser and i-Toyota.
rows.rewrite: Ungalithinti ibhakili le-seatbelt. Sithembe.

rows.en: Stars out, load shedding can't touch this.
rows.reason: 'Akukwazi lokhu' means 'can't do/manage this', not 'can't touch this', and 'ukucisha' alone leaves load shedding unclear; natives use the loan 'i-load shedding'.
rows.rewrite: Izinkanyezi zikhona, i-load shedding ayikwazi ukuzithinta.

rows.en: The clouds are committed to being average.
rows.reason: 'Azibophezele ekubeni phakathi naphakathi' is correct and its formal 'commitment' register is the joke; 'phakathi naphakathi' is a real word for average.

rows.en: This is the weather you'll miss in December traffic.
rows.draft: Lesi yisimo sezulu ozosithanda ethrafikhini kaDisemba.
rows.reason: 'Ozosithanda' means 'you will love it', not 'you will miss it'; the verb for miss/remember is 'ukukhumbula' (as in the confirmed 'ukhumbula umbhede wakho').
rows.rewrite: Lesi yisimo sezulu ozosikhumbula ethrafikhini kaDisemba.

rows.en: The kind of cold that has you Googling 'underfloor heating Bloemfontein'.
rows.draft: Uhlobo lwamakhaza olukwenza ugcine usu-Google'a 'underfloor heating Bloemfontein'.
rows.reason: 'Ugcine usu-Google'a' is an awkward, translated-sounding verbing of Google; a speaker says 'ufune ku-Google ...'.
rows.rewrite: Uhlobo lwamakhaza olukwenza ufune ku-Google 'underfloor heating Bloemfontein'.

rows.en: At least it's not raining. That's the bar.
rows.reason: 'Akulini' is a wrong form (not raining is 'akuni'), and 'yilokho okukhona' says 'that's what there is', losing the 'that's the low bar' punch.
rows.rewrite: Okungenani akuni. Yilokho kuphela esikulindele.

rows.en: Thunder rolling in. Inside is the move.
rows.reason: 'Hlala phakathi' reads as 'stay in the middle'; 'inside' is 'ngaphakathi' (as in the confirmed 'hlala ngaphakathi'), and 'inside is the move' loses its casual tone.
rows.rewrite: Ukuduma kuyeza. Kungcono uhlale ngaphakathi.

rows.en: The world got a soft filter this morning.
rows.reason: Natural and correct; 'ifilitha' is the word natives kept elsewhere, and 'ethambile ekuseni' gives the soft-morning image.

rows.en: Slip-slops, shorts, sun. The trinity.
rows.draft: Izimbadada, amabhulukwe amafushane, ilanga. Inhlangano emithathu.
rows.reason: 'Inhlangano emithathu' means 'three organisations' and has the wrong concord (would be 'ezintathu'); the 'trinity' punchline is lost and reads oddly. The first beat is fine.
rows.rewrite: Izimbadada, amabhulukwe amafushane, ilanga. Ziphelele lezi zintathu.

rows.en: Wet conditions, probably. Don't quote us at the braai.
rows.reason: 'Okosa' has no locative, so 'at the braai' is not expressed; natives say 'braai' as a loan or use a locative phrase.
rows.rewrite: Izimo ezimanzi, cishe. Ungasicaphuni e-braai.

rows.en: Good night, South Africa.
rows.reason: 'Hamba kahle' means go well (a farewell to someone leaving), not good night; a speaker would say 'Lala kahle'. The rest reads fine.
rows.rewrite: Lala kahle, Ningizimu Afrika.

rows.en: Frost on the lawn. Frost on the bakkie. Frost in the pet bowl.
rows.draft: Isithwathwa otshanini. Isithwathwa ku-bakkie. Isithwathwa ku-pet bowl.
rows.reason: 'ku-pet bowl' is an English loan where isiZulu has its own phrase (natives replaced 'bird feeder' and 'milk bottle' the same way), and 'ku-bakkie' should take the e- locative. The three-beat repetition works.
rows.rewrite: Isithwathwa otshanini. Isithwathwa ebakkie. Isithwathwa esitsheni senja.

rows.en: The umbrella tax is now in effect.
rows.reason: 'isiyasebenza' has the wrong concord (si- is class 7; 'intela' is class 9) and is stiff for 'now in effect'; a speaker would say 'seyiqalile ukusebenza'.
rows.rewrite: Intela yesambulela seyiqalile ukusebenza.

rows.en: Rain so heavy it should pay rent.
rows.draft: Imvula enzima kakhulu kufanele ikhokhe irenti.
rows.reason: The 'so heavy that' link is missing, so the two clauses just sit side by side; natives use 'kangangokuthi' (as in their cooler-box line). 'enkulu' reads more naturally than 'enzima' for heavy rain.
rows.rewrite: Imvula enkulu kangangokuthi kufanele ikhokhe irenti.

rows.en: Time to dig out that ugly beanie.
rows.reason: 'ukumba' is literal digging in the ground; for taking something out of a cupboard a speaker says 'ukukhipha'. 'Isikhathi sokumba' is also stiffer than 'sekuyisikhathi'.
rows.rewrite: Sekuyisikhathi sokukhipha leyo beanie embi.

rows.en: This weather needs a life coach.
rows.draft: Lesi simo sezulu sidinga umqeqeshi wempilo.
rows.reason: Literal but natural, with 'umqeqeshi wempilo' for life coach; the deadpan personification of the weather survives.

rows.en: The Weber's been waiting all week for this.
rows.reason: 'loku' is not 'this' (it is 'lokhu'), and 'wait for' needs the applicative 'ilindele'; as written it reads garbled. The Weber waiting all week is a good image.
rows.rewrite: I-Weber ibilokhu ilindele lokhu isonto lonke.

rows.en: Your breath is doing special effects.
rows.reason: 'Umphefumulo' reads as soul or spirit before it reads as breath, so the cold-morning image is lost. 'I-special effects' also pairs a singular i- with a plural English word.
rows.rewrite: Ukuphefumula kwakho kwenza ama-special effect.

rows.en: This is the day the brochure was talking about.
rows.reason: 'Lolu usuku' and 'incwajana' (brochure) are correct, and the class 11 'ngalo' agrees; a clean, dry line.

rows.en: The neighbours' pool has never looked so tempting.
rows.draft: Ipuli yomakhelwane ayikaze ibukeke ihehekayo kangaka.
rows.reason: Natural: 'ayikaze ibukeke ihehekayo kangaka' carries 'never looked so tempting', and 'ipuli yomakhelwane' is the everyday loan.

rows.en: The frogs have entered the chat.
rows.reason: 'Amasele angene engxoxweni' keeps the join-the-conversation image and fits frogs croaking after rain.

rows.en: Probably cold. Take the jersey, you'll thank us.
rows.reason: Plain, warm and idiomatic: 'ijezi' is the right word and 'uzosibonga' lands the aside.

rows.en: Some cloud, some sun. The ratio's anyone's guess.
rows.draft: Amafu akhona, ilanga likhona. Isilinganiso siwukuqagela.
rows.reason: Understood and natural; the 'anyone's guess' flavour is a little thinner in 'siwukuqagela' but the dry shrug comes through.

rows.en: Ja, it's jersey weather. Double jersey.
rows.draft: Yebo, yisikhathi sejezi. Ijezi ephindwe kabili.
rows.reason: 'Yisikhathi sejezi' with 'ijezi ephindwe kabili' reads naturally and keeps the double-jersey beat.

rows.en: Can't see a thing. Not a thing.
rows.reason: Exactly how a speaker says it: 'Angiboni lutho. Lutho.'

rows.en: At least the garden's happy. Someone has to be.
rows.draft: Okungenani ingadi iyajabula. Othile kumele ajabule.
rows.reason: 'Okungenani' is right, and 'Othile kumele ajabule' is a little formal but natural enough; the rueful second beat works.

rows.en: Rooibos consumption just doubled.
rows.reason: 'Ukusetshenziswa' means usage, as of a tool, not drinking tea; a speaker would say 'ukuphuza irooibos'. It reads like a report.
rows.rewrite: Ukuphuza i-rooibos kusanda kuphindeka kabili.

rows.en: The moon's doing the most tonight.
rows.reason: 'Yenza konke' says the moon does everything; 'doing the most' means showing off, so the joke is lost. Natives used 'siziqhayisa' for the sky showing off.
rows.rewrite: Inyanga iyaziqhayisa kakhulu namuhla ebusuku.

rows.en: Weekend vibes so strong they need their own playlist.
rows.draft: I-weekend vibes ezinamandla kakhulu zidinga i-playlist yazo.
rows.reason: Concords are muddled: 'i-weekend vibes' takes a class 9 prefix but a class 10 verb, and the 'so strong that' link is missing. Natives write 'ama-vibes' and 'kangangokuthi'.
rows.rewrite: Ama-vibes e-weekend anamandla kangangokuthi adinga i-playlist yawo.

rows.en: Warm enough to leave the window open. Brave enough?
rows.reason: Natural and dry. 'Ukuvula' is slightly short of 'leave open', but the brave-enough closing beat lands.

rows.en: Nobody's posting this sunset on Instagram.
rows.reason: 'Lokhu' has nothing to point at, so the sunset is lost and the line doesn't say what nobody will post. A speaker names it: 'ukushona kwelanga'.
rows.rewrite: Akekho ozoposta ukushona kwelanga kwanamuhla ku-Instagram.

rows.en: Karoo morning. The kind that makes you respect every farmer who chose this.
rows.draft: Ekuseni eKaroo. Uhlobo olwenza uhloniphe wonke umlimi okhethe lokhu.
rows.reason: Reads as native: 'uhlobo olwenza uhloniphe' mirrors the confirmed 'uhlobo olwenza' pattern, and the respect for the farmer comes through.

rows.en: Windows closed, kettle on, and wait.
rows.reason: Several slips: 'avalwe' should be 'avaliwe', 'iketile' is 'iketela' (class 5, as in the confirmed 'iketela lisebenza'), and 'ivuliwe' (opened) is not 'on'. A speaker would use the telegraphic imperatives.
rows.rewrite: Vala amafasitela, bilisa iketela, bese ulinda.

rows.en: The car's heater is the most important relationship in your life right now.
rows.draft: I-heater yemoto yiyona relationship ebaluleke kakhulu empilweni yakho njengamanje.
rows.reason: 'yiyona relationship' leaves the loan bare and stiff; a speaker would say 'ubudlelwano' (or at least 'i-relationship') and put the car heater at the end of the sentence. The joke itself carries.
rows.rewrite: Ubudlelwano obubaluleke kakhulu empilweni yakho njengamanje yi-heater yemoto.

rows.en: Nobody told the forecast. It just arrived.
rows.reason: 'Sivele safika' hangs on the nearest noun, isibikezelo, so it reads as the forecast that arrived, not the weather; 'otshele' also drops the object concord (ositshelile).
rows.rewrite: Akekho ositshelile isibikezelo. Izulu lifike nje.

rows.en: Layer up like you're climbing Sani Pass.
rows.draft: Gqoka izingubo eziningi njengokukhwela uSani Pass.
rows.reason: 'Gqoka izingubo eziningi' is the confirmed phrase and Sani Pass lands for a KZN reader; at most a native might make 'uSani' into 'iSani'.

rows.en: Rain's possible. So is being completely wrong.
rows.draft: Imvula iyenzeka. Nokungabi yikho nhlobo kuyenzeka.
rows.reason: 'Nokungabi yikho nhlobo' is stiff and reads as 'it might not be rain at all', which loses the self-deprecating 'we may be completely wrong'; the natives' 'Kungenzeka' is the usual way to say possible.
rows.rewrite: Kungenzeka ine imvula. Kungenzeka futhi siphutha ngokuphelele.

rows.en: The car seats are freezing. Everything is freezing.
rows.draft: Izihlalo zemoto ziyaqanda. Yonke into iyaqanda.
rows.reason: 'ziyaqanda' is the natural word for things freezing, and the flat repetition keeps the deadpan.

rows.en: The morning forgot to render.
rows.reason: 'kukhohliwe' is a passive form; the app's own verb is 'khohlwe' (Ukhohlwe, sebakhohlwe). As written nobody forgets, so the morning is not the character. 'ukurenda' is a tech loan like 'bafura' and can stay.
rows.rewrite: Ukusa kukhohlwe ukurenda.

rows.en: Partly cloudy, partly guessing.
rows.reason: Impersonal 'kuqagela' has no one guessing; a speaker would say 'siqagela' (we are guessing). The 'kancane, kancane' pair keeps the two-beat turn.
rows.rewrite: Kunamafu kancane, siqagela kancane.

rows.en: Perfect weather for pretending you'll go to bed early.
rows.draft: Isimo sezulu esihle sokuzenza uzolala kusenesikhathi.
rows.reason: 'ukuzenza uzolala' is bare and stiff; a speaker would say 'ukuzenza sengathi uzolala'. 'kusenesikhathi' for early works.
rows.rewrite: Isimo sezulu esihle sokuzenza sengathi uzolala kusenesikhathi.

rows.en: A hoodie and an attitude. That's today.
rows.reason: Natural code-switched 'i-hoodie', 'isimo sengqondo' is the app's own word for attitude, and 'Namuhla kunje' closes it dry.

rows.en: Solidarity to everyone with one wet shoe right now.
rows.draft: Ukuhlangana nabo bonke abanesicathulo esisodwa esimanzi manje.
rows.reason: 'Ukuhlangana' means meeting or coming together, not solidarity, so it now says 'meeting everyone with one wet shoe'. The app's own word for fellow-feeling is 'zwela' (sikuzwela).
rows.rewrite: Siyabazwela bonke abanesicathulo esisodwa esimanzi manje.

rows.en: The dams are doing a happy dance.
rows.reason: 'Amadamu' is the everyday loan and 'umdanso ojabulayo' is plain and warm; the picture of happy dams comes through.

rows.en: Somewhere out there is the road. We think.
rows.reason: 'Endaweni ethile ngaphandle kunomgwaqo. Sicabanga.' has the same shape as the kept 'Endaweni ethile' fog lines, and the short second beat is the turn.

rows.en: Highveld winter: the only place where you wear two jackets to fetch the post.
rows.draft: I-Highveld winter: indawo lapho ugqoka ama-jacket amabili uyolanda iposi.
rows.reason: 'indawo' drops the 'only' (kuphela) that carries the joke; 'ama-jacket' where the app says 'ijazi', and 'I-Highveld winter' leaves 'winter' in English where the natives wrote 'ebusika'/'yasebusika'.
rows.rewrite: Ubusika base-Highveld: yindawo kuphela lapho ugqoka amajazi amabili ukuyolanda iposi.

rows.en: The sky's having a full-on tantrum.
rows.reason: 'Isibhakabhaka sithukuthele' is natural and warm; the child-tantrum flavour is thinner than in the English, but the angry sky comes through.

rows.en: The sky's giving absolutely nothing.
rows.reason: Short, natural 'asiniki lutho'; 'absolutely' is missing but the flat, dry tone reads the same as the kept 'Nothing to see here' lines.

rows.en: The commute just became a team sport.
rows.reason: 'umdlalo weqembu' is a clean team sport; 'uhambo' is the journey rather than the daily commute, but the traffic-chaos joke still reads.

rows.en: Your out-of-office is doing the heavy lifting.
rows.reason: 'I-out-of-office' is the same loan the kept sun line uses and 'yenza umsebenzi onzima' is natural, if a bit plainer than 'heavy lifting'.

rows.en: The streetlights are trying their best.
rows.reason: 'Izibani zomgwaqo' and 'zizama ngakho konke' read as natural effort for a personified light; understood at once.

rows.en: The car coughed twice before it agreed to start.
rows.draft: Imoto ikhwehlele kabili ngaphambi kokuvuma uku-starta.
rows.reason: 'ikhwehlele kabili' is the right cough and 'uku-starta' follows the same loan-verb pattern as the kept 'i-startile'; the stubborn car lands.

rows.en: Perfect day. No excuses. Get out.
rows.reason: Short and snappy; 'Akukho zaba' uses the right negative form and the app's own word for excuses, and 'Phuma' is a clean imperative.

rows.en: Driving slow is not a suggestion.
rows.reason: Natural and dry: 'Ukushayela kancane akusona isiphakamiso' carries the stern-but-wry tone of the English.

rows.en: The pool is not optional.
rows.reason: 'alikho ukukhetha' is not a way to say optional: 'alikho' means 'it is not there', so the line reads as 'the pool is not there, to choose'. A speaker makes going to the pool the thing that is not a choice.
rows.rewrite: Ukuya epulini akukona ukukhetha.

rows.en: Probably brewing something. Stay close to a roof.
rows.draft: Cishe kukhona okuphekwayo. Hlala eduze nophahla.
rows.reason: 'kukhona okuphekwayo' works as a 'something is brewing' idiom and 'Hlala eduze nophahla' is the confirmed storm line.

rows.en: The kids still going to school in shorts. They know things we don't.
rows.draft: Izingane zisaya esikoleni ngama-shorts. Ziyazi izinto thina esingazazi.
rows.reason: Plain and idiomatic; 'ngama-shorts' is a normal code-switch and the dry turn 'Ziyazi izinto thina esingazazi' lands like the English.

rows.en: Respect the thunder. It's earned it.
rows.reason: 'Kukufanele' is ambiguous (ku- can be 'you' or 'it') and never says the thunder has earned respect; name the respect with a yi- object concord.
rows.rewrite: Hlonipha ukuduma. Kuyayifanelekela inhlonipho.

rows.en: Eskom wishes it had this power.
rows.reason: 'U-Eskom' is a slip: the app writes company and place names with i- (i-Toyota, i-Free State, and 'i-Eskom' in the sister Eskom line); the 'amandla' power pun still works.
rows.rewrite: I-Eskom iyafisa ukuba namandla anje.

rows.en: Ponytail holders are doing overtime.
rows.reason: Descriptive Zulu for a hair tie that is understood at once, and 'zisebenza ngokweqile' keeps the overworked-object joke.

rows.en: The fynbos is loving it. You should too.
rows.reason: 'Iyakuthanda' can be heard as 'loves you' and 'Nawe kufanele' hangs with no verb; say plainly that the fynbos is happy and you should be too.
rows.rewrite: Ifynbos iyajabula. Nawe kufanele ujabule.

rows.en: Your makeup has an expiry date of 9am.
rows.draft: I-makeup yakho inesikhathi esiphelelayo sangu-9 ekuseni.
rows.reason: Stiff and translated: 'inesikhathi esiphelelayo sangu-9' is not how expiry is said; a speaker says it 'iphelelwa yisikhathi' at 'ngo-9'.
rows.rewrite: I-makeup yakho iphelelwa yisikhathi ngo-9 ekuseni.

rows.en: Lightning's putting on a show — watch from the window.
rows.reason: Natural; Umbani, bukela and iwindi are all in the natives' own lines (the confirmed one says 'umbukiso' for show, but 'umboniso' is fine).

rows.en: Calm night, most likely. The sky reserves the right to change.
rows.reason: 'Ubusuku obuzolile, cishe' and 'singashintsha' mirror the confirmed hedged lines (Kubukeka kuzolile. Cishe. / Iqiniso lingahluka); dry and natural.

rows.en: Days like this should come with a soundtrack.
rows.reason: 'Kufanele zize ne-soundtrack' is grammatical (kufanele plus subjunctive) and 'soundtrack' is a loan people just say.

rows.en: Hot-ish, likely. Keep the water close.
rows.reason: 'Cishe' covers both 'probably' and 'almost', so 'hot-ish, likely' comes through; plain, warm advice with 'eduze' as in the natives' roof line.

rows.en: The braai is cancelled. Yes, really.
rows.reason: 'Kukhanselelwe' has an extra applicative -el- (reads 'cancelled on/for someone'); the plain passive perfect is 'kukhanselwe'. 'Ukosa' for braai is right.
rows.rewrite: Ukosa kukhanselwe. Yebo, ngempela.

rows.en: The kind of day Joburg pretends it doesn't have until you're standing in it.
rows.draft: Uhlobo losuku iJoburg ezenza sengathi alukho, kuze kube usume phakathi kwalo.
rows.reason: 'Usume' is not a form of ukuma (stand); the subjunctive is 'ume'. The long clause is also heavy and stiff.
rows.rewrite: Uhlobo losuku iJoburg ezenza sengathi alukho, kuze kube ume phakathi kwalo.

rows.en: Tan lines are not a personality trait.
rows.reason: 'Imigqa yokushisa' is 'heat lines', not tan lines, and 'ubuntu' means humanity or kindness, not a personality trait; both halves misfire, like the flip-flop calque the natives threw out.
rows.rewrite: Imigqa yokushiswa yilanga akusona isimilo sakho.

rows.en: Your hairstyle? Gone. Accept it.
rows.reason: Three short beats that read as a speaker's own: 'Sihambile' and a bare 'Yamukela' (the same imperative the natives kept in the beige line).

rows.en: Eskom-friendly weather. No solar today.
rows.draft: Isimo sezulu esilungele i-Eskom. Akukho solar.
rows.reason: 'Esilungele i-Eskom' carries 'Eskom-friendly' and i-Eskom is the right form; only 'namuhla' is missing after 'Akukho solar', a small slip.

rows.en: Probably a clear night. The stars haven't confirmed.
rows.reason: 'Azikaqinisekisi' (not yet confirmed) is correctly formed and personifies the stars neatly; 'obuhle' for clear matches the natives' 'Cishe izulu lihle'.

rows.en: Your steering wheel is a hot plate.
rows.reason: Concrete and funny; 'isitsha esishisayo' (hot dish) gives the hot-plate image, and the steering-wheel loan is one a speaker would accept.

rows.en: Africa's sky just hits different.
rows.reason: 'Sihlukile' looks like a malformed 'sahlukile' (hluka means to strip or peel), and 'different' alone loses the positive 'hits different' sense; 'asifani nalutho' says nothing like it.
rows.rewrite: Isibhakabhaka sase-Afrika asifani nalutho.

rows.en: Wet socks. The ultimate betrayal.
rows.reason: Short and dry; 'amasokisi amanzi' is natural and 'ukukhaphela' (turn on someone) carries the betrayal, though 'dayisa' is the natives' confirmed betray word.

rows.en: Outside has betrayed you and you went anyway.
rows.draft: Ngaphandle kukukhaphele futhi noma kunjalo uhambile.
rows.reason: Bare 'Ngaphandle' as the subject matches the natives' own 'Ngaphandle ukuhlolwa kwesimilo'; 'kukukhaphele' is correctly formed, if slightly clunky.

rows.en: The ceiling fan is doing its best, but its best is not enough.
rows.draft: Ifeni yophahla yenza okusemandleni ayo, kodwa okusemandleni ayo akwanele.
rows.reason: Grammatical and keeps the deliberate 'best ... best' repetition; 'okusemandleni ayo' is a recognised idiom for 'what it can'.

rows.en: The sun is personally attacking you.
rows.reason: 'Likuhlasela wena mathupha' is idiomatic and funny: 'mathupha' is exactly 'personally', and the sun as aggressor fits the doctrine.

rows.en: The braai is happening. The braai always happens. We just pull the chairs closer.
rows.draft: I-braai iyenzeka. I-braai ihlala yenzeka. Sidonsa nje izihlalo zisondele.
rows.reason: Natural braai-always-happens deadpan; 'sidonsa nje izihlalo zisondele' reads like something a person would say, with i-braai kept as the loan.

rows.en: Lightning's putting Eskom's grid to shame.
rows.reason: 'ubeka i-Eskom ehlazweni' is a calque of 'put to shame'; a speaker would say uhlaza / wenza ihlazeke. The idea comes through, the grid is dropped.
rows.rewrite: Umbani wenza i-Eskom ihlazeke.

rows.en: Tomorrow's weather is tomorrow's problem.
rows.reason: 'sinkinga' has the copula wrong: with inkinga it needs 'siyinkinga' (or plain 'yinkinga'). The dry shrug otherwise lands.
rows.rewrite: Isimo sezulu sakusasa siyinkinga yakusasa.

rows.en: Your driveway is a mystery novel right now.
rows.draft: Indlela yakho yokungena iyinoveli yemfihlo manje.
rows.reason: 'indlela yokungena' for driveway and 'inoveli yemfihlo' for a mystery novel are plain and understandable; the fogged-in driveway image carries.

rows.en: Watch for fog — it likes to arrive unannounced.
rows.draft: Qaphela inkungu — ithanda ukufika ingazange yazise.
rows.reason: 'Qaphela inkungu' plus 'ingazange yazise' is a natural way to say it arrives without warning; the personified fog works.

rows.en: Rain on the way, give or take.
rows.reason: Same 'luyeza, cishe' pattern as the confirmed 'give or take' heat line; a plain, natural forecast remark.

rows.en: Hail's down — cover the bakkie.
rows.reason: 'vala ibakkie' means shut the bakkie, not cover it; the confirmed corpus has isembozo for a cover, so use mboza.
rows.rewrite: Isichotho siyawa — mboza ibakkie.

rows.en: Could rain. Could just threaten to.
rows.reason: 'Kungana' / 'kungasongela nje' is short, natural potential-mood wording and keeps the weather-threatens idea.

rows.en: Your washing just moved to the neighbour's yard.
rows.draft: Izingubo zakho zisanda kuthuthela egcekeni likamakhelwane.
rows.reason: Izingubo is the washing, 'egcekeni likamakhelwane' has the right possessive, and 'zisanda kuthuthela' gives the off-hand moving-house joke.

rows.en: The neighbourhood cats have taken over.
rows.reason: 'amakati akhelwane' is wrong (neighbours' cats is 'amakati omakhelwane'), and 'asethathile' has no object, so 'taken over' is left hanging.
rows.rewrite: Amakati omakhelwane asethathe yonke indawo.

rows.en: Saturday energy: maximum. Responsibilities: minimum.
rows.reason: 'Amandla angoMgqibelo' is correct and the colon structure keeps the English deadpan; 'imisebenzi' is a loose but fine rendering of responsibilities.

rows.en: Sky's throwing rocks. Stay inside.
rows.reason: 'silahla amatshe' is a clear, natural picture of hail; 'phakathi' is understood though the confirmed form is 'ngaphakathi'.

rows.en: Save this one in the memory bank.
rows.reason: 'Gcina lolu suku enkumbulweni' is natural and warm; 'lolu' agrees with usuku.

rows.en: The fog arrived unannounced. Classic fog.
rows.reason: 'ingamenyiwe' means uninvited, not unannounced, and 'yoqobo' means authentic/the very thing rather than 'classic'; the natives used 'Okujwayelekile' for classic.
rows.rewrite: Inkungu ifikile ingazange yazise. Okujwayelekile.

rows.en: Fire up the Weber. It's the law.
rows.reason: 'Basa' is the right verb for lighting a fire, Weber stays as the brand, and 'Kungumthetho' is a natural deadpan.

rows.en: Mist building, maybe. Headlights wouldn't hurt.
rows.reason: 'Layita izibani' is a forced loan verb and a blunt command; the English is a soft 'wouldn't hurt', and khanyisa is the confirmed word for lighting up.
rows.rewrite: Inkungu iyakheka, mhlawumbe. Kungaba kuhle ukukhanyisa izibani.

rows.en: The fog ate the neighbourhood.
rows.reason: 'idle indawo' says the fog ate 'a place', and indawo alone is not the neighbourhood; it needs 'yonke'.
rows.rewrite: Inkungu idle indawo yonke.

rows.en: Everyone with a pool just became very popular.
rows.draft: Bonke abanepuli basanda kuba nesithunzi kakhulu.
rows.reason: 'nesithunzi' means with dignity/respect, not popular (the corpus uses isithunzi for dignity); the meaning is lost.
rows.rewrite: Bonke abanepuli sebethandwa kakhulu manje.

rows.en: Nature just reminded us of the pecking order.
rows.draft: Imvelo isanda kusikhumbuza ukuthi ubani ophambili.
rows.reason: Natural and understood; 'ubani ophambili' is a bit softer than the confirmed 'ongumphathi' but carries the pecking-order idea.

rows.en: The sun's bunking today.
rows.reason: 'ukubaleka' is used for skipping off, so the sun running away today reads naturally and the truant image comes through.

rows.en: Walking to the bin is now an expedition.
rows.reason: 'esikhongelweni' does not mean a bin and looks mangled (possibly from isikhongozelo); a plain loan, ibhini, is safer.
rows.rewrite: Ukuhamba uye ebhini lodoti manje kuwuhambo.

rows.en: Probably fog later. The Boland does this.
rows.draft: Cishe inkungu kamuva. I-Boland yenza lokhu.
rows.reason: Mirrors the confirmed 'Cishe kuyaqanda. I-Boland yenza lokhu ekuseni' pattern; 'Cishe inkungu kamuva' is natural.

rows.en: Your motivation froze on the way to the door.
rows.draft: Ugqozi lwakho luqande endleleni eya emnyango.
rows.reason: 'ugqozi' is the confirmed word for motivation, 'luqande' is right for frozen, and the sentence flows naturally.

rows.en: Walking to the car counts as a sun hazard today.
rows.draft: Ukuhamba uye emotweni kubhekwa njengengozi yelanga namuhla.
rows.reason: Stiff calque of 'counts as': 'kubhekwa njengengozi' is formal 'is regarded as', and 'ukuhamba uye emotweni' double-marks the going; a speaker would say it is simply a sun hazard.
rows.rewrite: Ukuya emotweni nje kuyingozi yelanga namuhla.

rows.en: Your suede shoes chose today? Bold.
rows.draft: Izicathulo zakho zesuede zikhethe namuhla? Isibindi.
rows.reason: Natural; the clipped 'Isibindi.' is a dry sarcastic remark and the suede loan sits comfortably.

rows.en: Perfect night to actually see the Milky Way.
rows.reason: 'iNdlela yoSisi' is not a name I can confirm for the Milky Way and reads as 'Sister's road'; do not coin it, use the loan i-Milky Way. 'ngempela' for 'actually' is also missing.
rows.rewrite: Ubusuku obuhle bokubona i-Milky Way ngempela.

rows.en: Grey skies, low conviction.
rows.reason: 'ukholo' means faith/belief, so 'ukholo oluphansi' reads as low religious faith, not low conviction; the joke lands wrong.
rows.rewrite: Izulu elimpunga, alizethembi kangako.

rows.en: Getting out of bed was a mistake. A documented one.
rows.reason: Reads naturally; 'elibhaliwe phansi' (written down) is an everyday idiom and the dry fragment carries the 'documented' turn.

rows.en: Braai weather, boet! No excuses.
rows.reason: 'Izulu lokosa' and 'Akukho zaba' are natural, 'izaba' is already in the confirmed lines, and boet stays as the usual code-switch.

rows.en: Bring a jacket. Or sunscreen. Or both.
rows.draft: Letha ijazi. Noma isivikelo selanga. Noma kokubili.
rows.reason: Plain, natural; ijazi and isivikelo selanga are confirmed words and the 'noma... noma kokubili' rhythm mirrors the English.

rows.en: Ice cream isn't a treat. It's survival.
rows.reason: 'isipho' means gift, not treat; 'yikuphila' is 'it is living', not survival (ukusinda).
rows.rewrite: I-ice cream akuyona into yokuzijabulisa nje. Kuwukusinda.

rows.en: A perfectly average sky doing perfectly average things.
rows.draft: Isibhakabhaka esiphakathi nendawo esenza izinto eziphakathi nendawo.
rows.reason: 'phakathi nendawo' is the confirmed idiom for in-between/average and the repeated phrase echoes the English; 'perfectly' is not carried but the repetition keeps the dryness.

rows.en: You could fry an egg on the N1.
rows.reason: 'ukubhaka' is bake; a speaker fries an egg with 'ukuthosa', so 'bake an egg' sounds off.
rows.rewrite: Ungathosa iqanda ku-N1.

rows.en: Table Mountain? What Table Mountain?
rows.reason: Natural dismissive 'Iyiphi...?' and the place name is kept as a loan; lands as the fog joke.

rows.en: Blue sky, warm breeze. The simple stuff.
rows.draft: Isibhakabhaka esiluhlaza, umoya ofudumele. Izinto ezilula.
rows.reason: Warm and simple; isibhakabhaka esiluhlaza is understood as blue sky and 'Izinto ezilula' lands the closing beat.

rows.en: Even the geyser is putting in extra hours.
rows.reason: Natural; 'amahora engeziwe' is correct overtime hours, 'ne-geyser' matches the confirmed geyser line, and the concord is right.

rows.en: The shade is working harder than you today.
rows.reason: Same 'usebenza ngamandla kunawe' structure natives kept in the kettle line; reads naturally and the personified shade lands.

rows.en: Sunscreen is not optional, boet.
rows.reason: 'ayikhona ukukhetha' is wrong: 'ayikhona' means 'it is not there', so the meaning is lost; also the app says 'isivikelo selanga' for sunscreen, not 'ikhrimu'.
rows.rewrite: Akukho ukukhetha ngesivikelo selanga, boet.

rows.en: The koppies look like a postcard. Your feet feel like ice blocks.
rows.draft: Ama-koppies abukeka njenge-postcard. Izinyawo zakho zizwakala njenge-ice blocks.
rows.reason: English phrases forced in where isiZulu has its own, the way natives fixed 'bird feeder' and 'milk bottle': 'i-postcard' is ikhadi leposi and 'i-ice blocks' carries an English plural after an isiZulu prefix; 'zizwakala' also reads as 'sound like' for feet.
rows.rewrite: Ama-koppie abukeka njengekhadi leposi. Izinyawo zakho zibanda njengamabhlokhi eqhwa.

rows.en: Probably grey. Could lift, could thicken.
rows.reason: Brisk and natural; 'Cishe kumpunga' echoes the confirmed 'Mpunga, cishe' and 'kungaphakama, kungajiya' carries lift versus thicken.

rows.en: The world just... disappeared.
rows.reason: Short, idiomatic; 'nje...' holds the beat and 'wanyamalala' is exactly vanished.

rows.en: Mixed bag out there. We're hedging.
rows.reason: 'Usuku oluxubene' is natural; 'Asiqinisekile' is a close, slightly flatter stand-in for hedging and still reads warm and honest.

rows.en: Tiny ice bombs falling. Indoors is the only plan.
rows.draft: Amabhomu eqhwa amancane ayawa. Phakathi yiyo kuphela inhlelo.
rows.reason: 'Amabhomu eqhwa' works, but 'Phakathi yiyo kuphela inhlelo' is stiff: bare 'phakathi' cannot be the subject; a speaker would say staying inside is the only plan.
rows.rewrite: Amabhomu amancane eqhwa ayawa. Ukuhlala ngaphakathi yisu elilodwa.

rows.en: The clouds RSVP'd 'maybe' and showed up anyway.
rows.draft: Amafu aphendule athi 'mhlawumbi' avele eza nje.
rows.reason: 'aphendule' loses the invitation (RSVP) and 'avele eza nje' is awkward; the app spells it 'mhlawumbe', not 'mhlawumbi'.
rows.rewrite: Amafu aphendula isimemo athi 'mhlawumbe', kodwa afika noma kunjalo.

rows.en: The duvet is calling and the duvet is winning.
rows.reason: 'iyabiza' and the repeated i-duvet mirror the English well; 'iyaphumelela' is understood as winning (iyanqoba would be slightly more usual).

rows.en: Could go misty. The dew point's flirting with it.
rows.reason: First half is natural, but the dew-point flirt is replaced by a bare 'Qaphela' (be careful), so the second beat and the joke are gone.
rows.rewrite: Kungaba nenkungu. Amazolo asondela kuyo.

rows.en: Visibility: basically zero.
rows.reason: Same "Ukubonakala: ..." frame the natives kept; "cishe iqanda" is the school/score word for zero, which the pack rules acceptable, and it reads dry.

rows.en: Breezy, probably. Maybe more.
rows.reason: "Kunomoya omncane, cishe" mirrors the confirmed "Kuyabanda, cishe"; agreement is right; "okwengeziwe" is a little bookish but the understated hedge comes through.

rows.en: Cold enough for soup. And a second soup.
rows.reason: "Kubanda ngokwanele kwesobho" is a stiff word-for-word 'cold enough of soup'; natives use "kangangokuthi" for 'cold enough that'. The second beat is fine.
rows.rewrite: Kubanda kangangokuthi kudingeka isobho. Nesobho lesibili.

rows.en: Some wind expected. Strength still TBC.
rows.reason: Forecast-bulletin register ("kulindeleke", "umoya othile") but natural for a hedge line, and "awakaqinisekiswa" matches the confirmed "asikaqinisekiswa".

rows.en: The traffic lights are vibing in the mist.
rows.reason: "Izibani zomgwaqo" is street lights, not traffic lights (amarobhothi), and "ziyavuma" means agree/consent, not vibing, so the joke is gone; "enkungu" is also not the usual locative.
rows.rewrite: Amarobhothi azijabulisa enkungwini.

rows.en: Everything looks like a film scene. A creepy one.
rows.draft: Yonke into ibukeka njengomfanekiso wefilimu. Eyesabekayo.
rows.reason: "Umfanekiso wefilimu" is a picture/image of a film, not a film scene (isigcawu); the confirmed horror-film line uses "yesabisayo" for creepy.
rows.rewrite: Yonke into ibukeka njengesigcawu sefilimu. Esesabisayo.

rows.en: Nobody signed up for this temperature.
rows.reason: "Akekho ozibhalisele ..." carries 'nobody signed up' cleanly and "izinga lokushisa" is the standard word for temperature; slightly calqued but a speaker would say it.

rows.en: The sky's giving everything today.
rows.reason: Plain, grammatical, warm; the slang 'giving' becomes a literal 'gives everything', which still reads as the sky delivering, like the other loose calques the natives kept.

rows.en: Looks wet. The models are fairly sure, not certain.
rows.draft: Kubukeka kumanzi. Amamodeli aqinisekile cishe, hhayi ngokugcwele.
rows.reason: Matches the confirmed "Kubukeka kunamafu" and "Siqinisekile cishe" pattern; "hhayi ngokugcwele" is a touch formal but the hedge about the models lands.

rows.en: Your shoes are about to have a bad day.
rows.reason: Natural and compact; the shoes get a day of their own, the same personifying move as the kept "Ilanga lisekhefu letiye".

rows.en: Your car seat is a weapon right now.
rows.reason: Same "... yisikhali" shape the natives kept for the car door; concords (isihlalo, semoto, sakho, siyisikhali) are all correct.

rows.en: The car is out there. Allegedly.
rows.reason: Follows the confirmed "Imoto yakho ikhona ngaphandle" line; "Kuthiwa nje" is a natural 'so they say' for 'allegedly'.

rows.en: You'll dry. Eventually. Probably.
rows.reason: Short three-beat fragments with the confirmed "ekugcineni" and "cishe"; "uzokoma" is understood as drying off in rain context.

rows.en: Sun's out. Don't be fooled. Nature is lying.
rows.draft: Ilanga liphumile. Ungakhohliswa. Imvelo iqamba amanga.
rows.reason: "Imvelo iqamba amanga" is a real idiom for telling lies and "Ungakhohliswa" is correct; reads like something a speaker wrote.

rows.en: Silent Hill vibes. Without the monsters. Hopefully.
rows.draft: I-Silent Hill vibes. Ngaphandle kwezimanga. Sithemba.
rows.reason: "Izimanga" means wonders/marvels, not monsters, so the line now says 'without the wonders'; "I-Silent Hill vibes" also takes a singular i- on a plural loan.
rows.rewrite: Ama-vibes ase-Silent Hill. Ngaphandle kwama-monster. Sithemba.

rows.en: Night looks calm. Models permitting.
rows.draft: Ubusuku bubukeka buzolile. Uma amamodeli evuma.
rows.reason: "Ubusuku bubukeka buzolile" has correct class 14 concords and "uma amamodeli evuma" has the right 'e-' concord for a uma-clause; a dry, natural close.

rows.en: Welkom-cold today. The kind that goes through three jerseys like they aren't there.
rows.draft: Kubanda okweWelkom namuhla. Amakhaza angena kuma-jersey amathathu sengathi awekho.
rows.reason: "Ama-jersey" where the app's own word is ijezi (amajezi), and natives write the possessive with the place as "okwase-Welkom"; the rest reads well.
rows.rewrite: Kubanda okwaseWelkom namuhla. Amakhaza angena emajezini amathathu sengathi awekho.

rows.en: The sky can't make up its mind. Join the club.
rows.reason: "Ukuzinquma" is off (the confirmed line is "ukunquma"), and "Joyina iklabhu" is a word-for-word 'join the club'; a speaker would say 'we're the same'.
rows.rewrite: Isibhakabhaka asikwazi ukunquma. Sinjalo nathi.

rows.en: Today's weather: still loading.
rows.reason: "Sisalayisha" is the same kind of loan verb as the kept "siyabafura" (buffering); clear, light and dry.

rows.en: Cloud cover with a side of who-cares.
rows.reason: "Nohlangothi" ('and the side', a body side) is a stiff version of 'a side of', and "lokuthi" has the wrong concord for uhlangothi (lwokuthi); "ubani onendaba" for who-cares is fine.
rows.rewrite: Amafu, kanye nokuthi 'ubani onendaba?'

rows.en: Visibility sponsored by nobody.
rows.reason: "Kuxhaswe ngubani. Muntu." reads 'sponsored by who. Person.'; the punchline for 'nobody' is broken and a reader would not get the joke.
rows.rewrite: Akekho oxhasa ukubonakala.

rows.en: Somewhere a roof is someone's new kite.
rows.reason: "Umkhumbi" means ship, a word the app has already got wrong for kite; the line now says the roof is a new ship and the wind image is lost (kite is ikhayithi).
rows.rewrite: Endaweni ethile uphahla luyikhayithi entsha yomuntu.

rows.en: Hotter than a bakkie dashboard at noon.
rows.reason: "Kushisa ukudlula ..." is a natural comparative, "i-dashboard yebakkie" code-switches the way natives do, and "emini" gives the noon beat.
